'''Mary Elizabeth Schaps''' ({{Langx|he|מלכה אלישבע שפס}}; born August 6, 1948), also known as '''Malka Elisheva Schaps''', is an Israeli-American mathematician. She is Professor of Mathematics and Dean of the Faculty of Exact Sciences at [[Bar Ilan University]]. She received her Ph.D. from [[Harvard University]], and has published in [[deformation theory]], [[group theory]], and [[representation theory]]. She is also a writer, authoring several novels under the pseudonym '''Rachel Pomerantz'''.

==Early and personal life==
Mary Elizabeth Kramer was born on August 6, 1948, in [[Cleveland, Ohio]], United States.<ref name="First Tablet">{{cite news |last1=Emont |first1=Jon |title=Israel's First Ultra-Orthodox Female Dean Paves the Way for Other Religious Women Studying Math and Science |url=https://www.tabletmag.com/jewish-life-and-religion/176341/malka-schaps-haredi-dean |access-date=14 February 2019 |work=Tablet Magazine |date=26 June 2014 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="First Haaretz">{{cite news |title=Malka Schaps Becomes First Female Haredi Dean at Israeli University |url=https://www.haaretz.com/israel-gets-first-female-haredi-dean-1.5343504 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180531035810/https://www.haaretz.com/israel-gets-first-female-haredi-dean-1.5343504 |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 31, 2018 |access-date=14 February 2019 |work=Haaretz |date=2 October 2013 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="long CV">{{cite web |title=CURRICULUM VITAE - Malka Elisheva Schaps |url=http://u.math.biu.ac.il/~mschaps/CV.html |website=Department of Mathematics and Computer Science |publisher=Bar-Ilan University |access-date=14 February 2019 |archive-date=13 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113032556/https://u.math.biu.ac.il/~mschaps/cv.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> From 1965 to 1969, she was educated at [[Swarthmore College]] in Pennsylvania, [[majoring]] in mathematics, philosophy and history, and graduating ''summa cum laude'' in 1969.<ref name="short CV">{{cite web |title=Malka Schaps' Home Page - Curriculum Vitae |url=http://u.math.biu.ac.il/~mschaps/cv.html |website=Department of Mathematics and Computer Science |publisher=Bar-Ilan University |access-date=14 February 2019 |archive-date=13 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113032556/https://u.math.biu.ac.il/~mschaps/cv.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> She then attended [[Harvard University]] as a mathematics graduate student: she completed her [[Master of Arts]] (MA) degree in 1971 and her [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) degree in 1972.<ref name="short CV" /> Her doctoral thesis was titled "Non-singular deformations of space curves, using determinantal schemes": her advisors were [[David Mumford]] and [[Heisuke Hironaka]].<ref name="long CV" />

She was brought up a [[Presbyterian]] and then a [[Unitarian Universalism]].<ref name="First Tablet" /> She became interested in Judaism, and [[Conversion to Judaism|formally converted]] to [[Conservative Judaism]] in college.<ref name="First Tablet" /><ref name="became" /> In 1968, she married David Schaps, a classics professor who was then also studying for a PhD at Harvard.<ref name="Family">{{cite web |title=Malka Schaps' Home Page - Family |url=http://u.math.biu.ac.il/~mschaps/family.html |website=Department of Mathematics and Computer Science |publisher=Bar-Ilan University |access-date=14 February 2019 |archive-date=13 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113032515/https://u.math.biu.ac.il/~mschaps/family.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. David Schaps |url=https://classics.biu.ac.il/en/node/531 |website=Department of Classical Studies |publisher=Bar-Ilan University |access-date=14 February 2019}}</ref> They both gradually felt more and more drawn to [[Orthodox Judaism]] and considered themselves [[Haredi Judaism|Haredi]] by the time they had completed their doctorates.<ref name="First Tablet" /><ref name="became" /> The couple made [[aliyah]] (moved to Israel) in 1972.<ref name="First Haaretz" />

Together, she and her husband had two children: this was a small family by Haredi standards, and they raised four more [[foster children]].<ref name="First Tablet" /><ref name="became" /> They live in [[Bnei Brak]], a Haredi city near Tel Aviv.<ref name="became" />

==Career==
Schaps had some teaching experience at Harvard University: she was [[teaching assistant]] from 1971 to 1972, and a [[lecturer]] at the 1975 [[Harvard Summer School]].<ref name="long CV" /> In 1972, having moved to Israel, she was appointed a lecturer in mathematics at [[Tel Aviv University]].<ref name="long CV" /><ref name="became">{{cite news |last1=WACHMANN |first1=DOREEN |title=PROFILE: How Mary became Prof Malka - then Rachel |url=https://www.jewishtelegraph.com/prof_343.html |access-date=14 February 2019 |work=Jewish Telegraph |date=2016}}</ref> In her second year in Israel the [[Yom Kippur War]] occurred: the change in language, culture and the threat to her new family were a shock.<ref name="First Tablet" /> In 1977, she moved to [[Bar-Ilan University]] as a [[senior lecturer]]: she was promoted to [[associate professor]] in 1991 and [[full professor]] in 2006.<ref name="short CV" /> She was the only female [[Haredi Judaism|Haredi]] professor in Israel.<ref name="First Haaretz" /> In October 2013, she was appointed [[Dean (education)|Dean]] of Exact Sciences at Bar-Ilan University: having been the only female Haredi professor, she now became the highest ranking Haredi woman in Israeli academia.<ref name="First Haaretz" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Bitton-Jackson |first1=Prof Livia |title=Professor Malka Schaps: Ultra-Orthodox Dean |url=https://www.jewishpress.com/sections/jewess-press/impact-women-history/professor-malka-schaps-ultra-orthodox-dean/2013/11/29/ |website=JewishPress.com |access-date=14 February 2019 |date=29 November 2013}}</ref> She stepped down as dean in 2015, and was made [[Professor Emeritus]] on retirement in 2016.<ref name="long CV" />
